symptom: PC1 in VLAN 10 cannot ping PC2 in VLAN 10 connected across an inter-switch trunk link.
topology_notes: Switch SW1 connected to Switch SW2 via GigabitEthernet0/1. Host PC1 on SW1 (Fa0/1, VLAN 10). Host PC2 on SW2 (Fa0/1, VLAN 10).
show_outputs:
SW1# show interfaces GigabitEthernet0/1 switchport
Name: Gi0/1
Administrative Mode: dynamic auto
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 1 (default)

SW1# show interfaces trunk
(No active trunk interfaces listed)
rule_findings: RULE-04-TRUNK-NOT-OPERATIONAL: Trunk Link Inactive / Static Access Mode on Gi0/1

expected_response.root_cause: Uplink interface GigabitEthernet0/1 is operating in static access mode on VLAN 1 instead of an 802.1Q trunk, dropping tagged VLAN 10 frames.
expected_response.explanation: Because DTP did not negotiate trunking, Gi0/1 defaulted to an access port in VLAN 1. VLAN 10 broadcast and unicast packets cannot traverse the uplink until trunk mode is explicitly enabled.

symptom: Branch PC (192.168.50.10) cannot reach Headquarter Server (10.0.0.100). Ping drops with request timed out.
topology_notes: Branch Router R-Branch connected to HQ-Core via Serial0/0/0 (172.16.0.0/30). R-Branch has default route. HQ-Core routing table is missing 192.168.50.0/24.
show_outputs:
HQ-Core# show ip route 192.168.50.0
% Subnet not in table

HQ-Core# show ip route
Gateway of last resort is not set
C 10.0.0.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
C 172.16.0.0/30 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0
rule_findings: RULE-05-MISSING-ROUTE: Gateway of last resort is not set / % Subnet not in table

expected_response.root_cause: HQ-Core router lacks a return route for Branch subnet 192.168.50.0/24 and has no gateway of last resort, resulting in asymmetric packet drop on reply.
evidence: Gateway of last resort is not set
expected_response.explanation: Packets from the branch reach HQ Server, but HQ-Core cannot route return traffic because 192.168.50.0/24 is missing from its routing table. Adding the static route via Serial next-hop 172.16.0.2 completes bidirectional reachability.

symptom: Clients in LAN (192.168.1.0/24) can ping Web Server (172.16.1.50) but web browser connection to port 80 fails immediately.
topology_notes: Router R1 filtering traffic between LAN (Gi0/0) and Web Farm (Gi0/1). Access-list 102 applied outbound on Gi0/1.
show_outputs:
R1# show access-lists 102
Extended IP access list 102
 10 permit icmp 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 host 172.16.1.50 (40 matches)
 (Implicit deny ip any any active at end)

R1# show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/1
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 ip address 172.16.1.1 255.255.255.0
 ip access-group 102 out

expected_response.root_cause: Extended ACL 102 permits only ICMP echo traffic; HTTP (TCP port 80) is dropped by the default implicit 'deny ip any any' rule.
evidence: (Implicit deny ip any any active at end)
expected_response.explanation: Cisco extended access lists end with an unwritten implicit deny rule. Because ACL 102 only explicitly permits ICMP, TCP SYN packets destined for port 80/443 match the implicit deny and are discarded.
